mechanism_narrative: A stable or declining federal funds rate indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is stable or declining (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts decline below 1200 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as equity investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when HOUST falls below 1200 (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline below 1200 thousand units and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals a simultaneous weakening in consumer demand and supply chain capacity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to recessionary fears.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST < 1200 and INDPRO < 100 (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY), a rise in the federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate profitability.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and FEDFUNDS rises (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A declining unemployment rate signals a tightening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE declines (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline below 100 index units signals a contraction in manufacturing output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of months when INDPRO falls below 100 (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5% and the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight monetary policy combined with a strong labor market, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to inflationary pressures and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 1.5 and UNRATE < 4.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 annual growth > 2.0%), a slowdown in GDP growth below 1.5% signals an impending economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors price in reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth > 2.0 and growth slows below 1.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs negative returns).
